about-headline: The bridge between academia and Bitcoin.
about-lead: BitPolito is a student team at Politecnico di Torino and one of Italy's leading Bitcoin initiatives. We create opportunities to learn, build and connect around Bitcoin technology.
about-mission-p1: Founded four years ago, BitPolito has grown rapidly while staying focused on a deeper understanding and awareness of Bitcoin. We explore its technological and social dimensions, avoiding financial topics.
about-mission-p2: Our work spans computer science and mathematical R&D, education through courses and events, industry conferences and educational content with a scientific approach and a youthful voice.
about-mission-p3: BitGeneration, our successful lecture series for high schools, offers a solid overview of Bitcoin. Internally, members train together, contribute to FOSS projects and gain hands-on experience on challenging real-world work.
about-mission-p4: Inspired by the Cypherpunk movement, we stand for freedom, privacy and open-source principles. We collaborate with institutions, businesses and organisations to advocate the free and responsible use of technology.
about-working-title: Practical ways to partner with BitPolito.
about-working-text: We shape each collaboration around your goals, the students involved and the impact you want to create.
about-area1-item1-text: Bring a general Bitcoin topic, your company's work, or a practical workshop to the Politecnico di Torino. BitPolito members can support the session.
about-area1-item2-text: We design ad-hoc competitions around a product or service, involving Politecnico students and external members.
about-area1-item3-text: Present your company, meet talent and organise talks, stands, workshops or recruitment meetings with the University.
about-area2-item1-text: Members can investigate issues, test for bugs, explore use cases and suggest new developments alongside your ongoing work.
about-area2-item2-text: An individual member or a dedicated sub-team can work directly with your company, following requests, quality standards and deadlines.
about-area2-item3-text: We help connect companies with Politecnico students for supervised six-month internships or three-month thesis projects.
about-area3-item1-text: We promote events across our channels, distribute promo codes and create content during the event for future editions.
about-area3-item2-text: We co-create content about topics of common interest, your product or service, or the company behind it.
about-area3-item3-text: Your logo can appear on agreed media; we can mention the company in articles, podcasts, videos and physical events.
about-partnerships-text: Talk to the team about an educational event, a technical project or a media partnership.

hk-apply-aria: Apply to the Agentic Dollars Hackathon
hk-ct-p1: A pitch competition and business-reality format for Bitcoin and freedom tech projects, now in its second season, promoted and funded by the Plan B VC Fund and the Plan B Foundation in Lugano.
hk-ct-p2: Twelve finalist projects pitch over two days in front of a board of judges, negotiating direct investment and competing for three prizes in incubation, acceleration and relocation services. The final is recorded and published as episodes, and every finalist gets mentorship, promotion and access to the Plan B network.
hk-wk-e1: Doors open, kickoff, teams start building
hk-wk-note: Meals are covered during the event. The detailed run of show goes out to confirmed participants before the weekend.
hk-jd-intro: Every judge scores each project from 1 to 5 on the five criteria below. We tell you upfront, so you can build for it.
hk-jd1-text: How real and correct the integration with RGB Protocol on Bitcoin is. Working transactions, not simulated.
hk-jd2-text: How much the model genuinely runs on device, and how central it is to the project. We look at how you use it, not at model size.
hk-jd3-text: Whether the project runs end to end, and how much substantial work was done during the hackathon hours.
hk-jd4-text: Whether it solves a real problem, for someone identifiable, with a reason to exist after Sunday.
hk-jd5-text: How usable and understandable the flow is for someone who did not build it. We judge the flow, not the aesthetics: clarity of steps, error handling, how intuitive it is for an outsider.
hk-jd-bonus-text: Using Tether WDK is optional, but a working integration earns extra points on top of your total, and a well-built, central integration earns the full bonus.
hk-faq1-q: Do I need to know Bitcoin already?
hk-faq1-a: No. Most people who apply have never used RGB or built on Bitcoin, and that is exactly who this weekend is for. We’ll publish recorded tutorials for all three tools before the event, and mentors will be on site both days. What matters is that you want to build something.
hk-faq2-q: Can I apply without a team?
hk-faq2-a: Yes, and a lot of people do. When compiling the form, tell us that you are applying solo, and we will help you find teammates before the event, or on the first morning. The teams are composed of two to four people.
hk-faq3-a: We read every application. We look for motivation and for a clear vision of what you want to build around AI and payment infrastructure, not for a long CV or years of experience. Places are limited to around 70, so tell us honestly what draws you here.
hk-faq4-q: Is it free? Are meals covered?
hk-faq4-a: The hackathon is free to attend. Lunch on Saturday, an afternoon coffee break and breakfast on Sunday are covered for all participants. You only cover your own travel and accommodation.
hk-faq5-q: Do I have to use RGB, QVAC and WDK?
hk-faq5-a: RGB and QVAC are required for every project. WDK is optional, but strongly encouraged: integrating self-custodial wallets earns bonus points during judging.
hk-faq6-a: Projects are judged by team members from Tether, KaleidoSwap and Utexo: the teams building on RGB, QVAC and WDK in production. Full judging lineup announced closer to the event.
hk-faq7-q: What kind of laptop do I need?
hk-faq7-a: Nothing exotic. The models we recommend for this hackathon are small and quantized, and run on an ordinary laptop. You only need one capable machine per team, not one each, and mentors are on site to help with setup. Recommended models and minimum specs come with the tutorials.
hk-faq8-q: Can I bring a project I already started?
hk-faq8-a: Yes, but we only judge what you build during the hackathon. Declare what already exists when you arrive, keep the weekend’s work in dated commits, and do the RGB and QVAC integration on site.
hk-faq9-q: What time does the event actually end on Sunday?
hk-faq9-a: Pitches start at 16:00 and we keep them tight, awards included, so everyone can head home at a reasonable hour. This decision is designed with train travelers in mind, so you shouldn’t need to worry about missing the last one of the day.
